name: Lev held-out protocol
status: Fixed study settings; existing aggregate results only

checkpoints.note: all trained on S31 (kev08b-release-mix + decision-v7 train replay); Lev-2.6B has seeds 0-2, every other model seed 0 only

reads.script: scripts/depth_rows.py --allow_test (the only use of --allow_test in the project), fp32, TF32 off, one record per pass
reads.overlong: records over a backbone's context are skipped and listed, as in every earlier read; comparisons use the questions every compared system read

panels.primary: eval-v1-test (9,740 questions; gates on the answerable, non-report-only rows pooled over its tiers)
report_only: eval-v1-test per tier, per source and per difficulty k
panels.not_locked: JevBench public (231) was read in phases 1-4; its earlier numbers may be quoted, it is not part of this read

temperatures: one per depth (one for a dense model), fitted on decision-v7 calibration (121-point log grid on 0.25..4, minimum NLL), frozen before the test rows are scored

stopper.xfit_note: the stopper is fitted on the calibration rows plus the other fold's unlabelled rows of the same test panel (label-free), as on development

gates.G1: adaptive accuracy - deepest accuracy >= -1 pp, paired 95% CI lower bound > -2 pp, question cost <= 0.70
gates.G2: adaptive - random escalation with the same stop distribution: paired 95% CI lower bound > 0
gates.G3: adaptive - fixed-depth frontier at the same question cost: paired 95% CI lower bound > 0
gates.ci: paired bootstrap over record groups, 2,000 resamples, seed 0
gates.verdict: per Lev checkpoint, on eval-v1-test (primary) and breadth-v1-test (secondary), each reported; for Lev-2.6B also the three seeds pooled (analysis/seed_pool.py: per question the seeds' correctness averaged, group bootstrap) and the per-seed count of seeds that pass. Where a gate fails, it is reported as is

cascades.script: analysis/cascade.py --axis latency, rules maxp and agree, as study
cascades.latency: Per-depth fits in results/latency/latency-fits.json; H200, bf16, batch one, measured on development requests and applied to token counts.
cascades.verdict: study's rule at matched mean latency: 'better than' a cascade when one of eval-v1-test / breadth-v1-test has CI lower bound > 0 and the other upper bound > 0; 'worse' when both upper bounds < 0; otherwise 'level'. Every Lev x cascade x rule is reported

supplementary: Lev-3B-depth3-s0: the same tables (G1-G3, per tier) under its own heading, not in the main table, not in any verdict
